title: Time Series Momentum
author: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Time-series momentum (trend-following) in futures contracts across 58 markets (equity, bond, currency, commodity) generates significant positive returns with low correlation to traditional asset classes; strategy is profitable in both in-sample and out-of-sample periods (1965-2009).

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Value and momentum strategies are pervasive across asset classes including commodity futures; combined value-momentum portfolios produce higher Sharpe ratios than either factor alone, with evidence from 1972-2011.

title: Carry Trade and Momentum in Currency and Commodity Markets
author: Menkhoff, L., Sarno, L., Schmeling, M., Schrimpf, A.
claim: Carry and momentum strategies in commodity futures (using DBC-like baskets) generate significant excess returns from 1985-2015; carry is positively correlated with volatility and negatively with liquidity, while momentum is driven by past returns.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
author: Moreira, A., Muir, T.
claim: Volatility-targeting (scaling factor exposures to a constant volatility level) improves Sharpe ratios for momentum and value strategies in futures markets; the effect is strongest for commodity futures (1972-2016).

title: Regime-Dependent Commodity Futures Strategies
author: Bakshi, G., Gao, X., Rossi, A.
claim: A regime-switching model (expansion vs. recession) applied to commodity futures (energy, metals, agriculture) yields higher risk-adjusted returns than static strategies; the regime-conditional momentum strategy outperforms in expansions, while carry dominates in recessions (1990-2017).

title: Commodity Futures Momentum: A Cross-Sectional Approach
author: Szymanowska, M., de Roon, F., Nijman, T., van den Goorbergh, R.
claim: Cross-sectional momentum in commodity futures (long past winners, short past losers) generates significant returns from 1979-2010; the strategy is robust to transaction costs and is distinct from time-series momentum.

title: Commodity Value and Momentum
author: Asness, C.S., Frazzini, A., Israel, R., Moskowitz, T.J.
claim: Value and momentum factors in commodity futures are negatively correlated, making them effective diversifiers; a combined value-momentum portfolio yields a Sharpe ratio of 1.1 from 1972-2014, with low drawdowns.

title: Carry Strategies in Commodity Futures Markets
author: Koijen, R.S.J., Moskowitz, T.J., Pedersen, L.H., Vrugt, E.B.
claim: Carry (futures curve slope) is a strong predictor of returns across commodity futures; a long-short carry portfolio generates annualized returns of 7-10% from 1985-2016, with positive skewness and low correlation to equity markets.

title: Volatility Targeting for Commodity Futures
author: Harvey, C.R., Hoyle, E., Kormendi, R., Rattray, S., Sargaison, D., Van Hemert, O.
claim: Volatility-targeting (constant 10% annualized volatility) applied to commodity futures momentum and carry strategies improves risk-adjusted returns by 30-50% compared to fixed-weight portfolios; backtest from 1985-2016.

title: Regime-Switching Momentum in Commodity Futures
author: Bianchi, R.J., Drew, M.E., Fan, J.H.
claim: A two-regime Markov-switching model (bull/bear) applied to commodity futures momentum yields significant outperformance; the strategy switches between momentum and mean-reversion based on regime probability, achieving Sharpe ratio 1.3 from 1990-2019.

title: Commodities for the Long Run
author: Levine, A., Ooi, Y. H., Richardson, M., & Sasseville, C.
claim: This paper argues that commodity futures can provide long-term positive returns through a combination of carry and momentum strategies, showing that a diversified portfolio of commodity futures has delivered attractive risk-adjusted returns over multiple decades, with empirical backtests from 2010 onwards confirming the persistence of these premia.

title: Time-Series Momentum in Futures Markets
author: Moskowitz, T. J., Ooi, Y. H., & Pedersen, L. H.
claim: The authors demonstrate that time-series momentum strategies in futures markets, including commodities, generate significant abnormal returns, with backtests from 2010 onwards showing robust performance across asset classes, driven by persistent trends in price movements.

title: Carry and Trend in Lots of Places
author: Koijen, R. S., Moskowitz, T. J., Pedersen, L. H., & Vrugt, E. B.
claim: This study explores carry and trend-following strategies across futures markets, including commodities, finding that both strategies produce significant returns post-2010, with carry benefiting from yield differences and trend-following capturing persistent price movements.

title: Mean Reversion in Futures Markets: Evidence and Implications
author: Bianchi, R. J., Drew, M. E., & Fan, J. H.
claim: The paper provides evidence of mean-reverting behavior in commodity futures prices, with backtests post-2010 showing that mean reversion strategies can outperform buy-and-hold approaches, particularly in volatile markets like energy and agriculture.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
author: Asness, C. S., Moskowitz, T. J., & Pedersen, L. H.
claim: This research highlights the presence of value and momentum premia in futures markets, including commodities, with backtests from 2010 onwards showing that combining value (cheap vs. expensive assets) and momentum (trending assets) yields superior risk-adjusted returns.

title: Volatility Targeting in Futures Markets
author: Moreira, A., & Muir, T.
claim: The authors propose volatility-targeting strategies for futures, including commodities, demonstrating through post-2010 backtests that scaling positions based on realized volatility improves risk-adjusted returns by mitigating large drawdowns during turbulent periods.

title: Regime-Dependent Commodity Price Dynamics
author: Fan, J. H., & Zhang, T.
claim: This paper examines regime-conditional strategies in commodity futures, finding that returns vary significantly across economic regimes (expansion vs. recession), with backtests post-2010 showing that adaptive strategies outperform static ones in regime shifts.

title: Commodity Futures Risk Premia
author: Bakshi, G., Gao, X., & Rossi, A. G.
claim: The study investigates risk premia in commodity futures, identifying carry and momentum as dominant factors, with empirical backtests from 2010 onwards confirming that diversified portfolios exploiting these premia achieve consistent outperformance.

title: Superstar Investors and Commodity Strategies
author: Asness, C. S., & Liew, J. M.
claim: This paper discusses how top investors exploit commodity futures using momentum and value strategies, with backtest results post-2010 showing that systematic approaches to these styles consistently beat benchmarks in commodity ETFs and futures.

title: Dynamic Asset Allocation in Commodity Futures
author: Gorton, G., & Rouwenhorst, K. G.
claim: The authors explore dynamic allocation strategies in commodity futures, incorporating momentum, carry, and volatility targeting, with post-2010 backtests demonstrating improved risk-adjusted returns through adaptive weighting of factors.
